authority: 2026-10-11 owner direct ratification: D24/D48/D96/D192/... are peers of D1-D9 (supersedes Number-only storage-tier interpretation of #2490)
rules: D24, D48, D96, D192, ... are first-class numeric DOMAINS with the same ontology rank as D1-D9.
The domain law is D(24 * 2^n), n >= 0; first width 24 and subsequent widths double.
A numeric object is exact bits + explicit numeric domain + admitted domain law, never an unqualified Number24 tier.
Equality of bit payload or mathematical magnitude cannot implicitly identify different domains; bridges require an independent law.
Numeric source literals and Text7 digits are optional surface projections, not semantic requirements.

For addition of two admitted nonnegative values in the SAME Dn numeric domain, compute the exact sum, including carry. If it fits n bits the result stays in Dn; if it needs n+1 bits it is admitted in next numeric domain D(2n), with all bits preserved. This is an explicit same-domain-addition bridge only.
Domain-qualified output retains its exact width, zero-filling unused high bits of the D(2n) word; zero-fill does not change its domain identity.

This law ratifies overflow promotion for same-domain natural addition ONLY; mixed-domain operators, negative values, fractions, multiplication/other operation promotion and implicit general widening remain deferred.
not_yet_ratified: mixed-domain implicit coercion and general widening
semantic_identity: exact numeric domain D(24*2^n) + exact binary domain word + admitted domain law
domain_residency_scope: numerical D24/D48/... exist as peer domains, plus exact same-domain natural-addition overflow promotion is ratified; other operations and general widening/bridges remain separate

addition_widening.scope: two nonnegative operands admitted in the same numeric domain Dn, n=24*2^k
addition_widening.selection: if sum < 2^n, result domain Dn; otherwise result domain D(2n)
addition_widening.representation: exactly domain-width binary bits; left zero-fill to output width, never truncate carry
addition_widening.deferred: mixed-domain operands; general coercion; multiplication promotion; signed/rational arithmetic
